content: The clinic collects only the personal and medical information necessary to provide safe and effective healthcare services, and this data is handled in accordance with applicable data protection regulations. Patient data is stored on encrypted servers accessible only to authorised clinical and administrative staff; no data is shared with third parties without explicit patient consent except where required by law or for direct care purposes such as laboratory referrals or specialist letters. Patients have the right to access, review, and request corrections to their health records by submitting a written request to the clinic's data protection officer. Medical records are retained for a minimum of seven years after the last consultation, or until the patient turns 25 in the case of minors, in line with regulatory requirements. Patients who believe their data has been mishandled may raise a concern with the clinic's data protection officer or lodge a complaint with the relevant regulatory authority.
